card: Quantization: divisor 3Ch on the load high byte; try other band schemes (different divisor, mask) that spread A, B and zombies better.

model.what: A005 phase-sim (partner crossfire only, no opponents/zombies) generalized to any band divisor; all 64x64 (hA,hB) load pages (step 4), 200k rounds. Env DIV, PA, PB.
model.results: Combos with A killed by B (of 4096): 3Ch 1650, 40h 0, 20h 0, 10h 1536, 30h 1392, 50h 1040. With divisor 40h or 20h the A-B anchor offset is always 1Ch + k*20h pages, which in the model never puts B's 800h trail across A's rebuilding worker. Real engine: partner deaths are only ~1-2% of deaths (A005 trace nd583), so the possible gain is <=~0.004 and not visible in screens.

candidates.label: d40
candidates.change: mov ch,03Ch -> mov ch,040h in all three quantizations (A startup, B startup, B zombie path). Same bytes count and timing. A targets 2C/6C/AC/EC pages, B 10/50/90/D0.
candidates.notes: Screen neutral; placement changes decorrelate pairing so the screen CI is ~+-0.039 (5x wider than for timing edits). Clearly loses vs LowKey (0/6 cohorts won; LowKey team 0.43 vs 0.17).

candidates.label: d20
candidates.change: mov ch,03Ch -> mov ch,020h in all three quantizations (8 bands; A target always 0Dh..2Ch pages above own load page). Timing identical.
candidates.notes: Screen ALL +0.0066 is far inside noise (CI +-0.033), 2025 group slightly negative, multi -0.047 (fails coordinator multi gate -0.02). Threat job: real opponent-specific trade-off (cgx +0.11 and zchain4 +0.10 vs LowKey -0.14, callfart -0.06), net ~0.

threatFindings.threat: Band divisor choice changes outcomes vs specific opponents (opponent-specific placement effects, not a uniform gain)
movsw_LowKey benefits when we leave divisor 3Ch: rev0's 3Ch band scheme is (by luck or design) favourable vs LowKey
threatFindings.evidence: Both non-3Ch schemes lose vs LowKey: screen cohorts -0.52 (d40) / -0.40 (d20); threat 7wyhs -0.375, threat 3vrga -0.138. Mechanism not traced (no budget left).

threatFindings.threat: Partner crossfire depends on band divisor (3Ch lets B's 800h trail kill A; 40h/20h never in the model)
threatFindings.evidence: band-sim.mjs only (3Ch 1650/4096 combos vs 0 for 40h/20h); real-engine partner deaths ~1-2% (A005 nd583); not measurable in screens 82nv3/yvvpq.

threatFindings.threat: Screen field S cannot resolve band-scheme changes: placement edits decorrelate the paired arms
threatFindings.evidence: Screen CI half-width 0.039 (82nv3) and 0.033 (yvvpq) vs ~0.01-0.016 for timing-only edits (A004 yx4ug/ujom1). Cohort-level screen effects that looked consistent across both screens (callfart +0.17/+0.24) did not replicate in an independent threat job (3vrga callfart -0.064).

recommendation: Do not promote. Keep divisor 3Ch. Band divisor 40h/20h is net neutral on the screen and trades opponents (d20: +cgx123123/+zchain4 vs -LowKey; d40: strongly -LowKey). Any further band-scheme work needs much larger, placement-robust evaluation (screen CI ~+-0.035) and a trace vs LowKey to understand why 3Ch is favourable there.
